definition: A word embedding technique that learns vector representations by factorizing a matrix of global word co-occurrence statistics.
details: GloVe (Global Vectors) combines the benefits of matrix-factorization and local context-window methods to produce embeddings that capture both global corpus statistics and local semantic relationships.

explainer.lead: GloVe turns patterns in how words occur together into numeric vectors. This gives computers a compact way to represent words and their relationships using statistics gathered across an entire corpus.

tiers.eli5: Imagine keeping a giant notebook of which words show up together, like noticing that “peanut butter” and “jelly” often share a sentence. GloVe studies the whole notebook and gives each word its own list of numbers. A computer can then compare those number lists instead of treating every word as an unrelated label.
tiers.practitioner: Apply GloVe by building a global co-occurrence matrix from a corpus and factorizing it to obtain word vectors. It is useful when you want representations informed by both corpus-wide statistics and local semantic relationships. Keep in mind that the vectors reflect the co-occurrence patterns in the corpus used to produce them.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, let X be a matrix of global word co-occurrence statistics; GloVe factorizes X to learn a vector representation for each word. The approach combines matrix factorization with advantages associated with local context-window methods. Its representations are consequently shaped by the co-occurrence evidence available in the training corpus.

explainer.example: Suppose “coffee” and “cup” often occur together in a corpus, while “coffee” and “bicycle” rarely do. The co-occurrence matrix records this difference, and factorization learns vectors that reflect the stronger association between “coffee” and “cup.”

usedIn.name: Natural language processing
usedIn.detail: Provides vector representations of words for computational language tasks.

usedIn.name: Semantic relationship analysis
usedIn.detail: Represents words using corpus statistics that capture local semantic relationships.

explainer.intuition: Words that occur together reveal something about how they are used. GloVe uses those patterns across an entire corpus, rather than looking only through a small local context window, to build word vectors.
howItWorks: Count how often words occur together across the corpus.
Organize those global counts into a word co-occurrence matrix.
Factorize the matrix to learn a vector for each word.
Use the vectors to represent global statistics and local semantic relationships.
explainer.whyItMatters: GloVe bridges two useful sources of information: corpus-wide co-occurrence statistics and local semantic relationships. The result is a word representation grounded in observed language use.
misconceptions: GloVe is not based only on local context windows; it factorizes global co-occurrence statistics.
Its vectors are learned numeric representations, not hand-written dictionary definitions.
